title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 4th District

context.text: Incumbent William Timmons (R) won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary. Courtney McClain's June 9, 2026 Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced without a primary contest.

candidates.name: William Timmons

summary.text: William Timmons is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th District, in office since January 2019 and seeking re-election. A former prosecutor and small business owner, he served in the South Carolina Senate from 2016 to 2019 and is a captain and Judge Advocate General officer in the South Carolina Air National Guard. In Congress he sits on the Financial Services and Oversight committees.

background.text: Born in Greenville, South Carolina, in 1984.

Earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University (2006), master's degrees from the University of South Carolina (2009) and New York University (2021), and a law degree from the University of South Carolina (2010).
Owned a small business and worked as a prosecutor in the Thirteenth Circuit Solicitor's Office.
Serves as a captain and Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer in the South Carolina Air National Guard.

Won the 2016 Republican primary runoff for South Carolina State Senate District 6, defeating incumbent Michael Fair with 65.3 percent, and won the November 2016 general election. He served in the State Senate until 2019.

Won the 2018 Republican primary runoff for the open 4th District seat over Lee Bright (54.3 percent to 45.7 percent), then won the November 2018 general election over Democrat Brandon Brown with 59.6 percent. He succeeded Trey Gowdy and took office January 3, 2019.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, including its Digital Assets subcommittee, and on the Oversight Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs and sits on the Delivering on Government Efficiency subcommittee.
Earlier House service included the Select Committee on the Modernization of Congress and the House Republican Steering Committee.
Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 65.8 percent over David Atchley and Robert Lee.

positions.summary: On his campaign site during the Biden administration (about 2021-22), he said he supported the border wall and would keep fighting to end catch-and-release policies and deport criminal illegal immigrants.
positions.quote: I supported President Trump’s border wall and will continue fighting to finish it, end catch-and-release policies, stop the flow of fentanyl, and deport criminal illegal immigrants.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (chairman of the Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee; also on the Delivering on Government Efficiency Subcommittee) and the Committee on Financial Services (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.researchNotes: No current-cycle Candidate Connection survey response or campaign-site issue statements were located within the research budget. Key floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Courtney McClain
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Democratic primary was canceled

summary.text: Courtney McClain, 25, of Spartanburg is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 4th District. A civil rights advocate, she became a political organizer at 19 and later led the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division. The Post and Courier reports her campaign centers on affordability, including health care, housing, public schools, infrastructure and voting rights.

background.text: Born in South Carolina and graduated from Spartanburg High School; The Post and Courier describes her as a Spartanburg native.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of South Carolina, Columbia (2023) and a graduate degree from Howard University (2025).

According to her Ballotpedia survey, she has received training from the Clyburn Fellow Program, the Emerge South Carolina Candidate Program and the Martin Luther King Jr. Center for Non-Violent Social Change, and worked in Washington, D.C., with the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation and Congressional Black Caucus Institute as an intern and fellow.
Became a political organizer at 19 and served as president of the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division, according to The Post and Courier.

By age 21 had testified at the Statehouse on gun violence, education, criminal justice reform, voting rights and women's reproductive rights, according to The Post and Courier; her Ballotpedia survey describes speaking before both the state House and Senate on these topics.
Is affiliated with the NAACP and Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated.

Launched her congressional campaign on March 18, 2026, and advanced from a canceled Democratic primary. The Post and Courier reports she has spoken at meetings and to county council members about a proposed data center in Spartanburg.

According to her Ballotpedia survey, she would be the youngest and first Black woman to run for the 4th District seat; The Post and Courier says she would be the first Black woman elected to Congress from South Carolina if she wins.

priorities.text: Tackling the housing crisis, protecting and expanding healthcare access, and fully funding public education.
Says she is passionate about voting rights, education, criminal justice reform, affordable housing, and healthcare.

positions.summary: Her campaign site lists universal background checks, secure storage, ghost gun regulation and crime gun tracing among her plans.
positions.quote: Closing the Charleston loophole and passing comprehensive legislation requiring universal background checks, secure storage, ghost gun regulation, and crime gun tracing

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for a national tenants' protection act to cap rent hikes and ban no-cause evictions.
positions.quote: Pass a national tenants' protection act to cap rent hikes, expand the right to counsel in housing court, and ban no-cause evictions.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would expand Medicare and support Medicare for All.
positions.quote: Expand Medicare and support Medicare for All to replace private insurance companies and ensure all South Carolinians have guaranteed healthcare coverage.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she opposes restrictions on abortion rights and would ensure access to reproductive care.
positions.quote: Oppose the dangerous restrictions placed on women's right to choose by ensuring equal and safe access to reproductive care within South Carolina and across the U.S.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would raise the federal minimum wage and end the tipped minimum wage.
positions.quote: End the tipped minimum wage and raise the federal minimum wage to a family-sustaining level that increases annually with the cost of living.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would push back against the Trump tariffs.
positions.quote: Push back against the nonsense Trump Tariffs that are increasing the prices of everyday goods and harming hard-working Americans' ability to afford necessary items.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would co-sponsor a War Powers Resolution to restore Congress's authority.
positions.quote: Co-sponsor a War Powers Resolution to end Trump's abuse of the military for personal gain and restore Congress's constitutional authority.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would push for an arms embargo on Israel.
positions.quote: push for an arms embargo on Israel and international accountability for a permanent ceasefire

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would end detention and deportation as a default and invest in legal support and integration.
positions.quote: End detention and deportation as a default by investing in housing, legal support, and integration and divesting from private prison contracts.

statements.quote: Fully fund the childcare voucher program and increase the pay of childcare workers.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from the issue pages of her campaign website (mcclainforsc.com), accessed Oct. 19, 2026, and her 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No stated position found on climate, school choice, voter citizenship proof, transgender sports, police funding, or zoning.

candidates.name: Jessica Ethridge
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated at the Libertarian Party convention

summary.text: Jessica Ethridge is the Libertarian Party nominee for South Carolina's 4th District. She was the Libertarian candidate for lieutenant governor in 2022, and her campaign then described her as active in the Libertarian Party and a legal professional. Little other biographical information about her 2026 campaign is public.

background.text: Was the Libertarian candidate for South Carolina Lieutenant Governor in 2022 on a ticket with gubernatorial candidate Bruce Reeves, receiving 1.2 percent of the vote.

According to her 2022 campaign, she had been active in the liberty movement for nearly a decade, a member of the South Carolina Libertarian Party since 2019, a state representative to two national conventions, Greenville County party secretary and State Committee 2nd Vice Chair; the campaign described her as an activist, mother and legal professional.
Advanced from the Libertarian convention for the 4th District on April 11, 2026.

priorities.text: Cost of living: cutting wasteful federal spending, reducing inflation-driving policies and removing unnecessary regulations.
National debt: identifying and eliminating wasteful federal spending and supporting policies that reduce the debt.
War and foreign policy: a foreign policy focused on peace, accountability and putting Americans first.

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign site (jessica4sc.com, Oct. 19, 2026) lists three issue areas (cost of living, war and foreign policy, national debt) in general terms; none takes a side on a listed guide issue. No Ballotpedia 2026 survey, forum or questionnaire answers found. A 2022 statewide-campaign site (as quoted by Ballotpedia) is not used.
